items.title: Jonathan Scales interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, December 23, 2025
items.q: The interviewee does not mention Vivaldi; Vivaldi is only mentioned by the interviewer in the context of playing on Spotify.

ctx.x: Yeah. I think that sometimes people will say things – I wish I could think of something right now that would be so cool, but yeah with instrumental music it’s all open to interpretation. So you know I do have to go back, “Can you tell me certain things is,” where my music has struck them in a certain way, and I always just take that like openly, because it’s open interpretation. But the craziest part for me is when someone hears my instrumental music and they come up and they express to me exactly what I was…

You know it’s interesting, I had an interesting experience today. My wife and I had on the Spotify channel for like Baroque music. So we had, you know Vivaldi and Bach were playing. And then I came in here to dub that piece, “The Questions Unanswerable” and it’s like whoa! Because the Baroque music, you mentioned architecture, and that’s the way I feel about that music is like it’s almost architecture in sound. And then I put that piece on and I just really, I connected with it from what I was hearing before.
